facts.fact: Dhanu's upper lake hut stands on scree above the far shore of the Mirror: split-deodar door, smoke hole, river-stone chulha, one sleeping shelf with a blanket, juniper and dung-cake stack, jars of barley meal, salt, dried apricots and tea.
facts.why: needed because the beat sets the night scene in a stone hut Dhanu has stocked with one chulha and one shelf

facts.fact: The pressure seam crossed on the Mirror is called the Sleeper's Spine in hill speech; Kunal gives it as the night's name and Ila writes it down.
facts.why: needed because the nightly name trade (F462) requires a name for the day's feature

facts.fact: Ila has carried the queen's letter sewn in her coat lining for six days and has decided not to open it yet, to see where Kunal's way goes first.
facts.why: needed because the beat says she does not open the letter, and gives her reason
